We had planned a family trip a couple months ago that includes a 4 hour flight. My husband can't go now because of work. I can't cancel because I bought it through one of those discount sites. I'll have a one year old and 2 1/2 year old. The 2 yrs has a ticketed seat, the 1 yrs is a lap child. I'm looking for logistical help. Are there any services that can help me get luggage from the car to the plane? Any other services or tips I should request or ask about seasoned flying parents?

(Note: if your response is to bitch about kids on the plane fuck off. I'm not posting to listen to your story about some insufferable parent that ruined your day once blah blah blah.....)
Any advice or tips on flying alone with two toddlers?

Don't

 

Gum

 

Take them to the park first to run them out so they sleep

Our original plan was to do 1/2 a day at Disneyland because our flight is a red eye (and we are annual pass holders at DL). I think that would be too ambitious alone. Bringing a friend might not be such a bad idea though.

If your husband can't go try to find a friend who would be willing to go on his ticket, who'd also be willing to help out a bit..

If you're taking a taxi to the airport, you might try talking to the taxi company about getting a driver to help with the luggage, they might even help carry it through the terminal for fee, doesn't hurt to ask.

If you want to hire a service that you intend to come with you through the entirety of your trip and help out, I can think of no services say for maybe a nanny, of course you would have to pay for their accommodations and such.

1. Get someone to drop you right off at the terminal. Then, most airports have sky caps and the other who will handle your bags. It will cost you $10-20 in tips, but worth it. If you must park, go find a skycap (or call ahead and ask how you can get one to come to the parking lot.)
  2. If you are renting a car, ask to rent car seats. Don't try to take your own!
  3. While you are waiting, don't be afraid to let your kids run in the airport. Find a corner and let them go crazy.
  4. If you need help loading, most airlines are pretty good about helping out.

On the flight:

  1. LOTS of snacks in small / separate bags. (Don't feed them much before the flight.)
  2. A couple new small toys that they haven't seen. Doesn't need to be expensive. Dollar store stuff will do wonders if they haven't seen it.
  3. I'm generally opposed to screen time for small kids but they can be wonderful in situations like this. A few kids apps on your phone can be great. (Again, don't let them spend time on it before the flight. You want 'new'. ) You might also want to invest in a backup battery / power bank for your phone / tablet. This can help keep the devices charged when you are on longer flights / airport waits.

There is a rhythm that you will find: toy / snack / screen / repeat.
